items.title: Harold E. Peterson Interview, 1979-08-06
items.q: So one day he said to me, he said, I want you to meet my mother.

ctx.x: Yeah, I made my first dollar playing music with him.

And then later he had no legs, Teddy. He had one leg, you see they used to play in front of, on Dauphin and Canal there, by Maison Blanche, for pickups. And of course, I used to, well, when I was playing over the Palisadean Lyric, I used to pass, I used to, oh, any time I was around there, I used to always go around and listen to them, they sound good. And he could make up songs and all, Gilbert, you know. So one day he said to me, he said, I want you to meet my mother. I said, gee, that's fine. So they were…
And, let's see, your father's people, they listed Ray Badu.
